sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Crawl4AI is an open-source Python web crawler that turns web pages into clean markdown and structured JSON for AI models. It runs a real browser, so it handles JavaScript-heavy pages, and you can use it as a library, a command-line tool or a Docker server.
sixtySeconds.problem: Web pages are full of menus, ads and scripts that waste an AI model's context. Crawl4AI fetches pages and returns just the useful content, with filters, citations and extraction schemas built in.
whoFor: Developers building RAG pipelines from web content
AI agent builders who need web reading
Python users who want a free, self-hosted crawler
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for a free Apache-2.0 crawler you fully control in Python, with LLM-ready markdown. The hosted Crawl4AI Cloud adds web search and handles bot walls for you, for a fee.
requirements: A Chromium browser, installed by crawl4ai-setup
Optional: an LLM API key for LLM extraction

overview: This repository is the Apache-2.0 crawler behind Crawl4AI Cloud. You install it with pip, run crawl4ai-setup once to install a browser, and then crawl pages from Python with AsyncWebCrawler or from the terminal with the crwl command.

Its markdown output keeps headings, tables and code, and filters such as BM25 and pruning remove boilerplate. For structured data it offers CSS and XPath extraction schemas that need no LLM, a schema generator, and LLM-based extraction with any provider.

You can also run it as a Docker server with a dashboard and playground on port 11235, secured with your own token. Crawl4AI Cloud is the hosted service with search, SERP and answer endpoints; the README says it includes 1,000 free credits a month.

install.verificationNote: Commands come from Crawl4AI's README. AIRepoHub hasn't run them yet.

steps.title: Create a token and start the server
steps.body: The server needs a token; without one it only answers inside its container.
steps.code:
export CRAWL4AI_API_TOKEN="$(openssl rand -hex 32)"
docker run -d -p 11235:11235 --name crawl4ai --shm-size=1g \
  -e CRAWL4AI_API_TOKEN="$CRAWL4AI_API_TOKEN" \
  unclecode/crawl4ai:latest

steps.title: Test it
steps.body: Allow about 10 seconds for it to start.

environment.name: CRAWL4AI_API_TOKEN
environment.description: Token that secures the self-hosted Docker server.

environment.name: CRAWL4AI_KEY
environment.description: Your Crawl4AI Cloud API key, only for the hosted service.

tutorial.title: Crawl your first page from Python
tutorial.useCase: Fetch a web page and print it as clean markdown.
setup: Crawl4AI installed and crawl4ai-setup run (see Installation)

steps.title: Save this as crawl.py
steps.code:
import asyncio
from crawl4ai import AsyncWebCrawler

async def main():
    async with AsyncWebCrawler() as crawler:
        result = await crawler.arun(url="https://news.ycombinator.com")
        print(result.markdown)

asyncio.run(main())

tutorial.expected: The script opens the page in a headless browser and prints the Hacker News front page as markdown.

troubleshooting.solution: Install it by hand with: python -m playwright install --with-deps chromium

troubleshooting.problem: Docker server refuses requests from outside
troubleshooting.solution: Set CRAWL4AI_API_TOKEN when starting it and send it as a Bearer token.
Questions need an LLM key; set it with crwl config.
